10.35.m: You are vigor, you are overpowering might, you are strength, you are brilliance, you are the abode and the name of the gods, you are the universe, you are all life, you are everything, you are all life, the victorious one. Om, I invoke the gāyatrī, I invoke the sāvitrī, I invoke Sarasvatī, I invoke the meter-seers, I invoke Śrī. For the gāyatrī, the meter is gāyatrī, Viśvāmitra is the seer, Savitṛ is the deity, Agni is the mouth, Brahmā is the head, Viṣṇu is the heart, Rudra is the tuft of hair, the earth is the womb, prāṇa, apāna, vyāna, udāna, and samāna [are the vital breaths], possessed of vital breath, white-colored, of the Sāṅkhyāyana lineage, the gāyatrī has twenty-four syllables, three feet, six bellies, five heads; the application is in the sacred thread ceremony. Om bhūḥ. Om bhuvaḥ. Om suvaḥ. Om mahaḥ. Om janaḥ. Om tapaḥ. Om satyam. Om: May we meditate upon that choice splendor of the god Savitṛ, who shall impel our thoughts. Om, water, light, sap, immortal, brahman, bhūr, bhuvas, suvar, om.

10.36.s: uttame śikhare jāte bhūmyāṃ parvatamūrdhani | brāhmaṇebhyo'bhyanujñātā gaccha devi yathāsukham | stuto mayā varadā vedamātā pracodayantī pavane dvijātā | āyuḥ pṛthivyāṃ draviṇaṃ brahmavarcasaṃ mahyaṃ dattvā prajātuṃ brahmalokam
10.36.d: उत्तमे शिखरे जाते भूम्यां पर्वतमूर्धनि । ब्राह्मणेभ्योऽभ्यनुज्ञाता गच्छ देवि यथासुखम् । स्तुतो मया वरदा वेदमाता प्रचोदयन्ती पवने द्विजाता । आयुः पृथिव्यां द्रविणं ब्रह्मवर्चसं मह्यं दत्त्वा प्रजातुं ब्रह्मलोकम्
10.36.m: Born on the highest summit, on the peak of the mountain on earth, / permitted by the brāhmaṇas, depart, O goddess, at your pleasure! / Praised by me, the boon-granting mother of the Vedas, inspiring in the wind, twice-born, / granting me lifespan on earth, wealth, and brāhmaṇical splendor, to go forth to the world of brahman!

10.37.s: ghṛṇissūrya ādityo na prabhā vātyakṣaram | madhu kṣaranti tadrasam | satyaṃ vai tadrasamāpo jyotī raso'mṛtaṃ brahma bhūrbhuvassuvarom
10.37.d: घृणिस्सूर्य आदित्यो न प्रभा वात्यक्षरम् । मधु क्षरन्ति तद्रसम् । सत्यं वै तद्रसमापो ज्योती रसोऽमृतं ब्रह्म भूर्भुवस्सुवरोम्
10.37.m: The heat of the sun, Āditya, does not cease to shine, the imperishable. They trickle honey, that essence. / Truth indeed is that essence: water, light, sap, immortal, brahman, bhūr, bhuvas, suvar, om.

10.38.s: brahmametu mām | madhumetu mām | brahmameva madhumetu mām | yāste soma prajā vathso'bhi so aham | duṣṣvapnahanduruṣṣaha | yāste soma prāṇāṃstāñjuhomi | trisuparṇamayācitaṃ brāhmaṇāya dadyāt | brahmahatyāṃ vā ete ghnanti | ye brāhmaṇāstrisuparṇaṃ paṭhanti | te somaṃ prāpnuvanti | āsahasrātpaṅktiṃ punanti | om
10.38.d: ब्रह्ममेतु माम् । मधुमेतु माम् । ब्रह्ममेव मधुमेतु माम् । यास्ते सोम प्रजा वथ्सोऽभि सो अहम् । दुष्ष्वप्नहन्दुरुष्षह । यास्ते सोम प्राणांस्ताञ्जुहोमि । त्रिसुपर्णमयाचितं ब्राह्मणाय दद्यात् । ब्रह्महत्यां वा एते घ्नन्ति । ये ब्राह्मणास्त्रिसुपर्णं पठन्ति । ते सोमं प्राप्नुवन्ति । आसहस्रात्पङ्क्तिं पुनन्ति । ओम्
10.38.m: May brahman come to me. May honey come to me. May brahman alone come to me as honey. O Soma, whatever offspring of yours is a calf, that am I. Slayer of bad dreams, unbearable to evil. Whatever vital breaths are yours, O Soma, those I offer. One should give the Trisuparṇa unasked to a brāhmaṇa. They indeed destroy the sin of slaying a brāhmaṇa, those brāhmaṇas who recite the Trisuparṇa. They attain Soma. / They purify a row up to a thousand. Om.

10.39.s: brahma medhayā | madhu medhayā | brahmameva madhu medhayā | adyā no deva savitaḥ prajāvathsāvīḥ saubhagam | parā duṣṣvapniyaṃ suva | viśvāni deva savitarduritāni parāsuva | yadbhadraṃ tanma āsuva | madhu vātā ṛtāyate madhu kṣaranti sindhavaḥ | mādhvīrnaḥ santvoṣadhīḥ | madhu naktamutoṣasi madhumatpārthivaṃ rajaḥ | madhu dyaurastu naḥ pitā | madhu mānno vanaspatirmadhumāṃ astu sūryaḥ | mādhvīrgāvo bhavantu naḥ | ya imaṃ trisuparṇamayācitaṃ brāhmaṇāya dadyāt | bhrūṇahatyāṃ vā ete ghnanti | ye brāhmaṇāstrisuparṇaṃ paṭhanti | te somaṃ prāpnuvanti | āsahasrātpaṅktiṃ punanti | om
10.39.d: ब्रह्म मेधया । मधु मेधया । ब्रह्ममेव मधु मेधया । अद्या नो देव सवितः प्रजावथ्सावीः सौभगम् । परा दुष्ष्वप्नियं सुव । विश्वानि देव सवितर्दुरितानि परासुव । यद्भद्रं तन्म आसुव । मधु वाता ऋतायते मधु क्षरन्ति सिन्धवः । माध्वीर्नः सन्त्वोषधीः । मधु नक्तमुतोषसि मधुमत्पार्थिवं रजः । मधु द्यौरस्तु नः पिता । मधु मान्नो वनस्पतिर्मधुमां अस्तु सूर्यः । माध्वीर्गावो भवन्तु नः । य इमं त्रिसुपर्णमयाचितं ब्राह्मणाय दद्यात् । भ्रूणहत्यां वा एते घ्नन्ति । ये ब्राह्मणास्त्रिसुपर्णं पठन्ति । ते सोमं प्राप्नुवन्ति । आसहस्रात्पङ्क्तिं पुनन्ति । ओम्
10.39.m: Brahman through wisdom. Honey through wisdom. Brahman alone as honey through wisdom. Today, O god Savitṛ, impel good fortune for us with offspring. Impel away bad dreams. / O god Savitṛ, drive away all misfortunes; impel toward us that which is auspicious. May the winds blow honey for him who observes the cosmic order; may the rivers flow honey; may the plants be sweet for us. May night be honey and morning; may the earthly realm be full of honey; may father sky be honey for us. May the lord of the forest be full of honey for us; may Sūrya be full of honey; may the cows be sweet for us. Whoever should give this Trisuparṇa unasked to a brāhmaṇa—they indeed destroy the sin of slaying an embryo, those brāhmaṇas who recite the Trisuparṇa. They attain Soma. / They purify a row up to a thousand. Om.

10.40.s: brahma medhavā | madhu medhavā | brahmameva madhu medhavā | brahmā devānāṃ padavīḥ kavīnāmṛṣirviprāṇāṃ mahiṣo mṛgāṇām | śyeno gṛddhrāṇāg svadhitirvanānāṃ somaḥ pavitramatyeti rebhann | haṃsaḥ śuciṣadvasurantarikṣasaddhotā vediṣadatithirduroṇasat | nṛṣadvarasadṛtasadvyomasadabjā gojā ṛtajā adrijā ṛtaṃ bṛhat | ṛce tvā ruce tvā samithsravanti sarito na dhenāḥ | antarhṛdā manasā pūyamānāḥ | ghṛtasya dhārā abhicākaśīmi | hiraṇyayo vetaso maddhya āsām | tasminthsuparṇo madhukṛtkulāyī bhajannāste madhu devatābhyaḥ | tasyāsate harayaḥ sapta tīre svadhāṃ duhānā amṛtasya dhārām | ya idaṃ trisuparṇamayācitaṃ brāhmaṇāya dadyāt | vīrahatyāṃ vā ete ghnanti | ye brāhmaṇāstrisuparṇaṃ paṭhanti | te somaṃ prāpnuvanti | āsahasrātpaṅktiṃ punanti | om
10.40.d: ब्रह्म मेधवा । मधु मेधवा । ब्रह्ममेव मधु मेधवा । ब्रह्मा देवानां पदवीः कवीनामृषिर्विप्राणां महिषो मृगाणाम् । श्येनो गृद्ध्राणाग् स्वधितिर्वनानां सोमः पवित्रमत्येति रेभन्न् । हंसः शुचिषद्वसुरन्तरिक्षसद्धोता वेदिषदतिथिर्दुरोणसत् । नृषद्वरसदृतसद्व्योमसदब्जा गोजा ऋतजा अद्रिजा ऋतं बृहत् । ऋचे त्वा रुचे त्वा समिथ्स्रवन्ति सरितो न धेनाः । अन्तर्हृदा मनसा पूयमानाः । घृतस्य धारा अभिचाकशीमि । हिरण्ययो वेतसो मद्ध्य आसाम् । तस्मिन्थ्सुपर्णो मधुकृत्कुलायी भजन्नास्ते मधु देवताभ्यः । तस्यासते हरयः सप्त तीरे स्वधां दुहाना अमृतस्य धाराम् । य इदं त्रिसुपर्णमयाचितं ब्राह्मणाय दद्यात् । वीरहत्यां वा एते घ्नन्ति । ये ब्राह्मणास्त्रिसुपर्णं पठन्ति । ते सोमं प्राप्नुवन्ति । आसहस्रात्पङ्क्तिं पुनन्ति । ओम्
10.40.m: Brahman through wisdom. Honey through wisdom. Brahman alone as honey through wisdom. Brahman among the gods, leader among the poets, seer among the inspired, buffalo among the beasts, falcon among the vultures, axe among the forests—Soma passes resoundingly through the purifier. / The swan dwelling in the pure, the Vasu dwelling in the intermediate space, the Hotṛ dwelling at the altar, the guest dwelling in the house, / dwelling among men, dwelling in the highest, dwelling in the cosmic order, dwelling in the sky, born of water, born of cows, born of the cosmic order, born of the rock, the great cosmic order. For the ṛc [I offer] to you, for light [I offer] to you; the streams of clarified butter flow together like milch cows, / purified within by the heart, by the mind; I behold the streams of clarified butter. / In their midst is the golden reed; therein the fair-winged bird, the honey-maker, nesting, sits bestowing honey upon the deities. On its bank sit the seven bay steeds, milking the svadhā, the stream of immortality. Whoever should give this Trisuparṇa unasked to a brāhmaṇa—they indeed destroy the sin of slaying a hero, those brāhmaṇas who recite the Trisuparṇa. / They attain Soma. They purify a row up to a thousand. Om.

10.41.s: medhā devī juṣamāṇā na āgādviśvācī bhadrā sumanasyamānā | tvayā juṣṭā nudamānā duruktānbṛhadvadema vidathe suvīrāḥ | tvayā juṣṭa ṛṣirbhavati devi tvayā brahmā gataśrīruta tvayā | tvayā juṣṭaścitraṃ vindate vasu sā no juṣasva draviṇo na medhe
10.41.d: मेधा देवी जुषमाणा न आगाद्विश्वाची भद्रा सुमनस्यमाना । त्वया जुष्टा नुदमाना दुरुक्तान्बृहद्वदेम विदथे सुवीराः । त्वया जुष्ट ऋषिर्भवति देवि त्वया ब्रह्मा गतश्रीरुत त्वया । त्वया जुष्टश्चित्रं विन्दते वसु सा नो जुषस्व द्रविणो न मेधे
10.41.m: May goddess Wisdom, being pleased, come to us, all-embracing, auspicious, and well-minded. / Cherished by you, driving away harsh words, may we speak mightily in the assembly, rich in heroic sons. Cherished by you, one becomes a seer, O goddess; by you a brāhmaṇa; and by you one who has attained glory. Cherished by you, one obtains manifold wealth; as such, be pleased with us, O Wisdom, like wealth.

10.42.s: medhāṃ ma indro dadātu medhāṃ devī sarasvatī | medhāṃ me aśvināvubhāvādhattāṃ puṣkarasrajā | apsarāsu ca yā medhā gandharveṣu ca yanmanaḥ | daivīṃ medhā sarasvatī sā māṃ medhā surabhirjuṣatāg svāhā
10.42.d: मेधां म इन्द्रो ददातु मेधां देवी सरस्वती । मेधां मे अश्विनावुभावाधत्तां पुष्करस्रजा । अप्सरासु च या मेधा गन्धर्वेषु च यन्मनः । दैवीं मेधा सरस्वती सा मां मेधा सुरभिर्जुषताग् स्वाहा
10.42.m:
May Indra grant me wisdom; may goddess Sarasvatī grant me wisdom. May both Aśvins, garlanded with blue lotuses, bestow wisdom upon me. That wisdom which is in the Apsarases, and that mind which is in the Gandharvas, the divine wisdom, Sarasvatī—may that fragrant wisdom be pleased with me, svāhā.

May fragrant Wisdom, multiform, golden-colored, moving, accessible to all, / vigor-filled, swelling with milk, may that fair-faced Wisdom be pleased with me.

10.43.s: ā māṃ medhā surabhirviśvarūpā hiraṇyavarṇā jagatī jagamyā | ūrjasvatī payasā pinvamānā sā māṃ medhā supratīkā juṣantām
10.43.d: आ मां मेधा सुरभिर्विश्वरूपा हिरण्यवर्णा जगती जगम्या । ऊर्जस्वती पयसा पिन्वमाना सा मां मेधा सुप्रतीका जुषन्ताम्

10.44.s: mayi medhāṃ mayi prajāṃ mayyagnistejo dadhātu mayi medhāṃ mayi prajāṃ mayīndra indriyaṃ dadhātu mayi medhāṃ mayi prajāṃ mayi sūryo bhrājo dadhātu
10.44.d: मयि मेधां मयि प्रजां मय्यग्निस्तेजो दधातु मयि मेधां मयि प्रजां मयीन्द्र इन्द्रियं दधातु मयि मेधां मयि प्रजां मयि सूर्यो भ्राजो दधातु
10.44.m: May Agni place wisdom in me, offspring in me, fiery brilliance in me. May Indra place wisdom in me, offspring in me, sensory power in me. May Sūrya place wisdom in me, offspring in me, radiant splendor in me.

10.45.s: apaitu mṛtyuramṛtaṃ na āganvaivasvato no abhayaṃ kṛṇotu | parṇaṃ vanaspaterivābhi naḥ śīyatāṃ rayissacatāṃ naḥ śacīpatiḥ
10.45.d: अपैतु मृत्युरमृतं न आगन्वैवस्वतो नो अभयं कृणोतु । पर्णं वनस्पतेरिवाभि नः शीयतां रयिस्सचतां नः शचीपतिः
10.45.m: May death depart; may immortality come to us; may the son of Vivasvat make fearlessness for us. Like a leaf from a tree, may wealth fall to us; may the lord of power accompany us.

10.46.s: paraṃ mṛtyo anu parehi panthāṃ yaste sva itaro devayānāt | cakṣuṣmate śṛṇvate te bravīmi mā naḥ prajāṃ rīriṣo mota vīrān
10.46.d: परं मृत्यो अनु परेहि पन्थां यस्ते स्व इतरो देवयानात् । चक्षुष्मते शृण्वते ते ब्रवीमि मा नः प्रजां रीरिषो मोत वीरान्
10.46.m: O Death, go along your own further path, which is other than the path of the gods. / To you who see and hear, I speak: do not harm our offspring, nor our heroic sons.

10.47.s: vātaṃ prāṇaṃ manasā'nvārabhāmahe prajāpatiṃ yo bhuvanasya gopāḥ | sa no mṛtyostrāyatāṃ pātvaṃhaso jyogjīvā jarāmaśīmahi
10.47.d: वातं प्राणं मनसाऽन्वारभामहे प्रजापतिं यो भुवनस्य गोपाः । स नो मृत्योस्त्रायतां पात्वंहसो ज्योग्जीवा जरामशीमहि
10.47.m: With our mind we reach out to the wind, the vital breath, and to Prajāpati, who is the guardian of the world. / May he protect us from death, guard us from distress; living long, may we attain old age.

10.48.s: amutrabhūyādadha yadyamasya bṛhaspate abhiśasteramuñcaḥ | pratyauhatāmaśvinā mṛtyumasmaddevānāmagne bhiṣajā śacībhiḥ
10.48.d: अमुत्रभूयादध यद्यमस्य बृहस्पते अभिशस्तेरमुञ्चः । प्रत्यौहतामश्विना मृत्युमस्मद्देवानामग्ने भिषजा शचीभिः
10.48.m: If from the other world, from the curse of Yama, O Bṛhaspati, you have delivered [us], / may the two Aśvins, the physicians among the gods, turn death away from us by their powers, O Agni.

10.49.s: hariṃ harantamanuyanti devā viśvasyeśānaṃ vṛṣabhaṃ matīnām | brahma sarūpamanu medamāgādayanaṃ mā vivadhīrvikramasva
10.49.d: हरिं हरन्तमनुयन्ति देवा विश्वस्येशानं वृषभं मतीनाम् । ब्रह्म सरूपमनु मेदमागादयनं मा विवधीर्विक्रमस्व
10.49.m: The gods follow the bay stallion as he carries off, the lord of all, the bull of thoughts. / Conformed to brahman, may this path come to me; do not cut off my way, take your stride.

10.50.s: śalkairagnimindhāna ubhau lokau sanemaham | ubhayorlokayorṛdhvā'ti mṛtyuṃ tarāmyaham
10.50.d: शल्कैरग्निमिन्धान उभौ लोकौ सनेमहम् । उभयोर्लोकयोरृध्वाऽति मृत्युं तराम्यहम्
10.50.m: Kindling Agni with splinters of wood, may I win both worlds. / Prospering in both worlds, I cross beyond death.

10.51.s: mā chido mṛtyo mā vadhīrmā me balaṃ vivṛho mā pramoṣīḥ | prajāṃ mā me rīriṣa āyurugra nṛcakṣasaṃ tvā haviṣā vidhema
10.51.d: मा छिदो मृत्यो मा वधीर्मा मे बलं विवृहो मा प्रमोषीः । प्रजां मा मे रीरिष आयुरुग्र नृचक्षसं त्वा हविषा विधेम
10.51.m: Do not cut me down, O Death, do not slay me, do not crush my strength, do not rob me. Do not harm my offspring, my lifespan, O fierce one; we would worship you, who observe men, with an oblation.

10.52.s: mā no mahāntamuta mā no arbhakaṃ mā na ukṣantamuta mā na ukṣitam | mā no vadhīḥ pitaraṃ mota mātaraṃ priyā mā nastanuvo rudra rīriṣaḥ
10.52.d: मा नो महान्तमुत मा नो अर्भकं मा न उक्षन्तमुत मा न उक्षितम् । मा नो वधीः पितरं मोत मातरं प्रिया मा नस्तनुवो रुद्र रीरिषः
10.52.m: Do not [harm] the great among us, nor the small among us, nor him who grows, nor him who has grown. / Do not slay our father, nor our mother; do not harm our dear bodies, O Rudra.

10.53.s: mā nastoke tanaye mā na āyuṣi mā no goṣu mā no aśveṣu rīriṣaḥ | vīrānmā no rudra bhāmito vadhīrhaviṣmanto namasā vidhema te
10.53.d: मा नस्तोके तनये मा न आयुषि मा नो गोषु मा नो अश्वेषु रीरिषः । वीरान्मा नो रुद्र भामितो वधीर्हविष्मन्तो नमसा विधेम ते
10.53.m: Do not harm us in our children, in our descendants, in our lifespan, nor in our cattle, nor in our horses. / In your anger do not slay our heroic sons, O Rudra; bearing oblations, we would worship you with reverence.

10.54.s: prajāpate na tvadetānyanyo viśvā jātāni pari tā babhūva | yatkāmāste juhumastanno astu vayaṃ syāma patayo rayīṇām
10.54.d: प्रजापते न त्वदेतान्यन्यो विश्वा जातानि परि ता बभूव । यत्कामास्ते जुहुमस्तन्नो अस्तु वयं स्याम पतयो रयीणाम्
10.54.m: O Prajāpati, none other than you has encompassed all these created things. Whatever we desire when offering to you, may that be ours; may we be masters of riches.

10.55.s: svastidā viśaspatirvṛtrahā vimṛdho vaśī | vṛṣendraḥ pura etu nassvastidā abhayaṃkaraḥ
10.55.d: स्वस्तिदा विशस्पतिर्वृत्रहा विमृधो वशी । वृषेन्द्रः पुर एतु नस्स्वस्तिदा अभयंकरः
10.55.m: Bestower of well-being, lord of the clan, slayer of Vṛtra, disperser of foes, the ruler, / may the bull Indra go before us, bestowing well-being, bringing fearlessness.

10.56.s: tryambakaṃ yajāmahe sugandhiṃ puṣṭivardhanam | urvārukamiva bandhanānmṛtyormukṣīya māmṛtāt
10.56.d: त्र्यम्बकं यजामहे सुगन्धिं पुष्टिवर्धनम् । उर्वारुकमिव बन्धनान्मृत्योर्मुक्षीय मामृतात्
10.56.m: We sacrifice to the three-eyed one, fragrant, increaser of nourishment. / Like a cucumber from its stalk, may I be released from death, not from immortality.

10.57.s: ye te sahasramayutaṃ pāśā mṛtyo martyāya hantave | tān yajñasya māyayā sarvānavayajāmahe
10.57.d: ये ते सहस्रमयुतं पाशा मृत्यो मर्त्याय हन्तवे । तान् यज्ञस्य मायया सर्वानवयजामहे
10.57.m: Whatever thousand and myriad snares of yours, O Death, are set for slaying mortals, / all those we cast off through the power of the sacrifice.

10.58.m: To Death, svāhā; to Death, svāhā.

10.59.s: devakṛtasyainaso'vayajanamasi svāhā | manuṣyakṛtasyainaso'vayajanamasi svāhā | pitṛkṛtasyainaso'vayajanamasi svāhā | ātmakṛtasyainaso'vayajanamasi svāhā | anyakṛtasyainaso'vayajanamasi svāhā | asmatkṛtasyainaso'vayajanamasi svāhā | yaddivā ca naktaṃ cainaścakṛma tasyāvayajanamasi svāhā | yathsvapantaśca jāgrataścainaścakṛma tasyāvayajanamasi svāhā | yathsuṣuptaśca jāgrataścainaścakṛma tasyāvayajanamasi svāhā | yadvidvāṃsaścāvidvāṃsaścainaścakṛma tasyāvayajanamasi svāhā | enasa enaso'vayajanamasi svāhā
10.59.d: देवकृतस्यैनसोऽवयजनमसि स्वाहा । मनुष्यकृतस्यैनसोऽवयजनमसि स्वाहा । पितृकृतस्यैनसोऽवयजनमसि स्वाहा । आत्मकृतस्यैनसोऽवयजनमसि स्वाहा । अन्यकृतस्यैनसोऽवयजनमसि स्वाहा । अस्मत्कृतस्यैनसोऽवयजनमसि स्वाहा । यद्दिवा च नक्तं चैनश्चकृम तस्यावयजनमसि स्वाहा । यथ्स्वपन्तश्च जाग्रतश्चैनश्चकृम तस्यावयजनमसि स्वाहा । यथ्सुषुप्तश्च जाग्रतश्चैनश्चकृम तस्यावयजनमसि स्वाहा । यद्विद्वांसश्चाविद्वांसश्चैनश्चकृम तस्यावयजनमसि स्वाहा । एनस एनसोऽवयजनमसि स्वाहा
10.59.m: You are the expiation of sin committed against the gods, svāhā. You are the expiation of sin committed against humans, svāhā. You are the expiation of sin committed against the fathers, svāhā. You are the expiation of sin committed by oneself, svāhā. You are the expiation of sin committed by another, svāhā. / You are the expiation of sin committed by us, svāhā. Whatever sin we have committed by day and by night, you are its expiation, svāhā. Whatever sin we have committed while sleeping and while awake, you are its expiation, svāhā. / Whatever sin we have committed in deep sleep and while awake, you are its expiation, svāhā. Whatever sin we have committed knowing and unknowingly, you are its expiation, svāhā. You are the expiation of every sin, svāhā.

10.60.s: yadvo devāścakṛma jihvayā guru manaso vā prayutī devaheḍanam | arā vāyo no abhi ducchunāyate tasmintadeno vasavo nidhetana svāhā
10.60.d: यद्वो देवाश्चकृम जिह्वया गुरु मनसो वा प्रयुती देवहेडनम् । अरा वायो नो अभि दुच्छुनायते तस्मिन्तदेनो वसवो निधेतन स्वाहा
10.60.m: Whatever grave offense against the gods we have committed with the tongue, or through negligence of mind, O gods, / on him who, as an enemy, plots evil against us, on him lay that sin, O Vasus, svāhā.

10.61.s: kāmo'kārṣīnnamo namaḥ | kāmo'kārṣītkāmaḥ karoti nāhaṃ karomi kāmaḥ kartā nāhaṃ kartā kāmaḥ kārayitā nāhaṃ kārayitā eṣa te kāma kāmāya svāhā
10.61.d: कामोऽकार्षीन्नमो नमः । कामोऽकार्षीत्कामः करोति नाहं करोमि कामः कर्ता नाहं कर्ता कामः कारयिता नाहं कारयिता एष ते काम कामाय स्वाहा
10.61.m: Desire did it: homage, homage! Desire did it; desire acts, not I; desire is the agent, I am not the agent; desire causes action, I do not cause action. This is yours, O desire, to desire, svāhā!

10.62.s: manyurakārṣīnnamo namaḥ | manyurakārṣīnmanyuḥ karoti nāhaṃ karomi manyuḥ kartā nāhaṃ kartā manyuḥ kārayitā nāhaṃ kārayitā eṣa te manyo manyave svāhā
10.62.d: मन्युरकार्षीन्नमो नमः । मन्युरकार्षीन्मन्युः करोति नाहं करोमि मन्युः कर्ता नाहं कर्ता मन्युः कारयिता नाहं कारयिता एष ते मन्यो मन्यवे स्वाहा
10.62.m: Anger did it: homage, homage! Anger did it; anger acts, not I; anger is the agent, I am not the agent; anger causes action, I do not cause action. This is yours, O anger, to anger, svāhā!

10.63.s: tilāñjuhomi sarasāṃ sapiṣṭāngandhāra mama citte ramantu svāhā | gāvo hiraṇyaṃ dhanamannapānaṃ sarveṣāg śriyai svāhā | śriyaṃ ca lakṣmiṃ ca puṣṭiṃ ca kīrtiṃ cā''nṛṇyatām | brahmaṇyaṃ bahuputratām | śraddhāmedhe prajāḥ saṃdadātu svāhā
10.63.d: तिलाञ्जुहोमि सरसां सपिष्टान्गन्धार मम चित्ते रमन्तु स्वाहा । गावो हिरण्यं धनमन्नपानं सर्वेषाग् श्रियै स्वाहा । श्रियं च लक्ष्मिं च पुष्टिं च कीर्तिं चा'ऽनृण्यताम् । ब्रह्मण्यं बहुपुत्रताम् । श्रद्धामेधे प्रजाः संददातु स्वाहा
10.63.m: I offer sesame seeds full of sap, ground, fragrant; may they delight in my mind, svāhā! / Cattle, gold, wealth, food and drink, for the prosperity of all, svāhā! / Prosperity and fortune and nourishment and fame and freedom from debt, / priestly status, having many sons, / may [he] grant faith, wisdom, and progeny, svāhā!

10.64.s: tilāḥ kṛṣṇāstilāḥ śvetāstilāḥ saumyā vaśānugāḥ | tilāḥ punantu me pāpaṃ yatkiñcidduritaṃ mayi svāhā || corasyānnaṃ navaśrāddhaṃ brahmahā gurutalpagaḥ | gosteyaṃ surāpānaṃ bhrūṇahatyā tilā śāntiṃ śamayantu svāhā || śrīśca lakṣmīśca puṣṭīśca kīrtiṃ cā''nṛṇyatām | brahmaṇyaṃ bahuputratām | śraddhāmedhe prajñā tu jātavedaḥ saṃdadātu svāhā
10.64.d: तिलाः कृष्णास्तिलाः श्वेतास्तिलाः सौम्या वशानुगाः । तिलाः पुनन्तु मे पापं यत्किञ्चिद्दुरितं मयि स्वाहा ॥ चोरस्यान्नं नवश्राद्धं ब्रह्महा गुरुतल्पगः । गोस्तेयं सुरापानं भ्रूणहत्या तिला शान्तिं शमयन्तु स्वाहा ॥ श्रीश्च लक्ष्मीश्च पुष्टीश्च कीर्तिं चा'ऽनृण्यताम् । ब्रह्मण्यं बहुपुत्रताम् । श्रद्धामेधे प्रज्ञा तु जातवेदः संददातु स्वाहा
10.64.m: Black sesame seeds, white sesame seeds, sesame seeds dedicated to Soma, obedient: / may the sesame seeds purify my sin, whatever misfortune is in me, svāhā! / The food of a thief, a new funeral feast, killing a brāhmaṇa, defiling the guru's bed, / theft of cows, drinking liquor, killing an embryo—may the sesame seeds bring peace and pacify [them], svāhā! / Prosperity and fortune and nourishment and fame and freedom from debt, / priestly status, having many sons, / may Jātavedas grant faith, wisdom, and understanding, svāhā!

10.65.s: prāṇāpānavyānodānasamānā me śudhyantāṃ jyotirahaṃ virajā vipāpmā bhūyāsaṃ svāhā | vāṅmanaścakṣuḥ śrotrajihvāghrāṇareto buddhyākūtiḥ saṃkalpā me śudhyantāṃ jyotirahaṃ virajā vipāpmā bhūyāsaṃ svāhā | tvakcarma māṃsa rudhira medo majjā snāyavo'sthīni me śudhyantāṃ jyotirahaṃ virajā vipāpmā bhūyāsaṃ svāhā | śiraḥpāṇi pāda pārśva pṛṣṭhorūdara jaṅgha śiśnopastha pāyavo me śudhyantāṃ jyotirahaṃ virajā vipāpmā bhūyāsaṃ svāhā | uttiṣṭha puruṣa harita piṅgala lohitākṣi dehi dehi dadāpayitā me śudhyantāṃ jyotirahaṃ virajā vipāpmā bhūyāsaṃ svāhā
10.65.d: प्राणापानव्यानोदानसमाना मे शुध्यन्तां ज्योतिरहं विरजा विपाप्मा भूयासं स्वाहा । वाङ्मनश्चक्षुः श्रोत्रजिह्वाघ्राणरेतो बुद्ध्याकूतिः संकल्पा मे शुध्यन्तां ज्योतिरहं विरजा विपाप्मा भूयासं स्वाहा । त्वक्चर्म मांस रुधिर मेदो मज्जा स्नायवोऽस्थीनि मे शुध्यन्तां ज्योतिरहं विरजा विपाप्मा भूयासं स्वाहा । शिरःपाणि पाद पार्श्व पृष्ठोरूदर जङ्घ शिश्नोपस्थ पायवो मे शुध्यन्तां ज्योतिरहं विरजा विपाप्मा भूयासं स्वाहा । उत्तिष्ठ पुरुष हरित पिङ्गल लोहिताक्षि देहि देहि ददापयिता मे शुध्यन्तां ज्योतिरहं विरजा विपाप्मा भूयासं स्वाहा
10.65.m: May my prāṇa, apāna, vyāna, udāna, and samāna breaths be purified; may I become light, free from dust, free from evil, svāhā! May my speech, mind, eye, ear, tongue, smell, semen, intellect, intention, and resolve be purified; may I become light, free from dust, free from evil, svāhā! May my outer skin, inner hide, flesh, blood, fat, marrow, sinews, and bones be purified; may I become light, free from dust, free from evil, svāhā! May my head, hands, feet, sides, back, thighs, belly, shanks, penis, lap, and anus be purified; may I become light, free from dust, free from evil, svāhā! Arise, O person, tawny, reddish-brown, red-eyed; give, give! May my prompter of giving be purified; may I become light, free from dust, free from evil, svāhā!

10.66.s: pṛthivyāpastejo vāyurākāśā me śudhyantāṃ jyotirahaṃ virajā vipāpmā bhūyāsaṃ svāhā | śabdasparśarūparasagandhā me śudhyantāṃ jyotirahaṃ virajā vipāpmā bhūyāsaṃ svāhā | manovākkāyakarmāṇi me śudhyantāṃ jyotirahaṃ virajā vipāpmā bhūyāsaṃ svāhā | avyaktabhāvairahaṃkārairjyotirahaṃ virajā vipāpmā bhūyāsaṃ svāhā | ātmā me śudhyantāṃ jyotirahaṃ virajā vipāpmā bhūyāsaṃ svāhā | antarātmā me śudhyantāṃ jyotirahaṃ virajā vipāpmā bhūyāsaṃ svāhā | paramātmā me śudhyantāṃ jyotirahaṃ virajā vipāpmā bhūyāsaṃ svāhā | kṣudhe svāhā | kṣutpipāsāya svāhā | viviṭṭyai svāhā | ṛgvidhānāya svāhā | kaṣotkāya svāhā | kṣutpipāsāmalaṃ jyeṣṭhāmalakṣmīrnāśayāmyaham | abhūtimasamṛddhiṃ ca sarvānnirṇuda me pāpmānaṃ svāhā | annamaya prāṇamaya manomaya vijñāna mayamānandamayamātmā me śudhyantāṃ jyotirahaṃ virajā vipāpmā bhūyāsaṃ svāhā
10.66.d: पृथिव्यापस्तेजो वायुराकाशा मे शुध्यन्तां ज्योतिरहं विरजा विपाप्मा भूयासं स्वाहा । शब्दस्पर्शरूपरसगन्धा मे शुध्यन्तां ज्योतिरहं विरजा विपाप्मा भूयासं स्वाहा । मनोवाक्कायकर्माणि मे शुध्यन्तां ज्योतिरहं विरजा विपाप्मा भूयासं स्वाहा । अव्यक्तभावैरहंकारैर्ज्योतिरहं विरजा विपाप्मा भूयासं स्वाहा । आत्मा मे शुध्यन्तां ज्योतिरहं विरजा विपाप्मा भूयासं स्वाहा । अन्तरात्मा मे शुध्यन्तां ज्योतिरहं विरजा विपाप्मा भूयासं स्वाहा । परमात्मा मे शुध्यन्तां ज्योतिरहं विरजा विपाप्मा भूयासं स्वाहा । क्षुधे स्वाहा । क्षुत्पिपासाय स्वाहा । विविट्ट्यै स्वाहा । ऋग्विधानाय स्वाहा । कषोत्काय स्वाहा । क्षुत्पिपासामलं ज्येष्ठामलक्ष्मीर्नाशयाम्यहम् । अभूतिमसमृद्धिं च सर्वान्निर्णुद मे पाप्मानं स्वाहा । अन्नमय प्राणमय मनोमय विज्ञान मयमानन्दमयमात्मा मे शुध्यन्तां ज्योतिरहं विरजा विपाप्मा भूयासं स्वाहा
10.66.m: May earth, water, fire, wind, and space for me be purified; may I become light, free from dust, free from evil, svāhā! May sound, touch, form, taste, and smell for me be purified; may I become light, free from dust, free from evil, svāhā! May the actions of my mind, speech, and body be purified; may I become light, free from dust, free from evil, svāhā! Through unmanifest states and through egos, may I become light, free from dust, free from evil, svāhā! May my self be purified; may I become light, free from dust, free from evil, svāhā! May my inner self be purified; may I become light, free from dust, free from evil, svāhā! May my supreme self be purified; may I become light, free from dust, free from evil, svāhā! To hunger, svāhā! To hunger and thirst, svāhā! To distress, svāhā! To the Ṛgveda rite, svāhā! To Kaṣotka, svāhā! I destroy the defilement of hunger and thirst, the elder misfortune; drive away from me misfortune, failure, and all evil, svāhā! May my self consisting of food, consisting of vital breath, consisting of mind, consisting of consciousness, and consisting of bliss be purified; may I become light, free from dust, free from evil, svāhā!

10.67.s: agnaye svāhā | viśvebhyo devebhyassvāhā | dhruvāya bhūmāya svāhā | dhruvakṣitaye svāhā | acyutakṣitaye svāhā | agnaye sviṣṭakṛte svāhā | dharmāya svāhā | adharmāya svāhā | adbhyassvāhā | oṣadhivanaspatibhyaḥ svāhā
10.67.d: अग्नये स्वाहा । विश्वेभ्यो देवेभ्यस्स्वाहा । ध्रुवाय भूमाय स्वाहा । ध्रुवक्षितये स्वाहा । अच्युतक्षितये स्वाहा । अग्नये स्विष्टकृते स्वाहा । धर्माय स्वाहा । अधर्माय स्वाहा । अद्भ्यस्स्वाहा । ओषधिवनस्पतिभ्यः स्वाहा
10.67.m: To Agni, svāhā! To all the gods, svāhā! To the fixed, the immense, svāhā! To the firm foundation, svāhā! To the unshakeable foundation, svāhā! To Agni Sviṣṭakṛt, svāhā! To dharma, svāhā! To adharma, svāhā! To the waters, svāhā! To herbs and trees, svāhā!

10.67.s: rakṣodevajanebhyassvāhā | gṛhyābhyassvāhā | avasānebhyassvāhā | avasānapatibhyassvāhā | sarvabhūtebhyassvāhā | kāmāya svāhā | antarikṣāya svāhā | yadejati jagati yacca ceṣṭati nāmno bhāgo'yaṃ nāmne svāhā | pṛthivyai svāhā | antarikṣāya svāhā
10.67.d: रक्षोदेवजनेभ्यस्स्वाहा । गृह्याभ्यस्स्वाहा । अवसानेभ्यस्स्वाहा । अवसानपतिभ्यस्स्वाहा । सर्वभूतेभ्यस्स्वाहा । कामाय स्वाहा । अन्तरिक्षाय स्वाहा । यदेजति जगति यच्च चेष्टति नाम्नो भागोऽयं नाम्ने स्वाहा । पृथिव्यै स्वाहा । अन्तरिक्षाय स्वाहा
10.67.m: To the rakṣas-folk and god-folk, svāhā! To the household [spirits], svāhā! To the settlements, svāhā! To the lords of the settlements, svāhā! To all beings, svāhā! To desire, svāhā! To intermediate space, svāhā! Whatever stirs in the world and whatever moves, this is the share of name; to name, svāhā! To the earth, svāhā! To intermediate space, svāhā!

10.67.s: dive svāhā | sūryāya svāhā | candramase svāhā | nakṣatrebhyassvāhā | indrāya svāhā | bṛhaspataye svāhā | prajāpataye svāhā | brahmaṇe svāhā | svadhā pitṛbhyassvāhā | namo rudrāya paśupataye svāhā
10.67.d: दिवे स्वाहा । सूर्याय स्वाहा । चन्द्रमसे स्वाहा । नक्षत्रेभ्यस्स्वाहा । इन्द्राय स्वाहा । बृहस्पतये स्वाहा । प्रजापतये स्वाहा । ब्रह्मणे स्वाहा । स्वधा पितृभ्यस्स्वाहा । नमो रुद्राय पशुपतये स्वाहा
10.67.m: To the sky, svāhā! To Sūrya, svāhā! To the moon, svāhā! To the lunar mansions, svāhā! To Indra, svāhā! To Bṛhaspati, svāhā! To Prajāpati, svāhā! To brahman, svāhā! Svadhā to the fathers, svāhā! Homage to Rudra, lord of beasts, svāhā!

10.67.s: devebhyassvāhā | pitṛbhyassvadhā'stu | bhūtebhyo namaḥ | manuṣyebhyo hantā | prajāpataye svāhā | parameṣṭhine svāhā | yathā kūpaḥ śatadhāraḥ sahasradhāro akṣitaḥ | evā me astu dhānyaṃ sahasradhāramakṣitam | dhanadhānyai svāhā | ye bhūtāḥ pracaranti divānaktaṃ balimicchanto vitudasya preṣyāḥ | tebhyo baliṃ puṣṭikāmo harāmi mayi puṣṭiṃ puṣṭipatirdadhātu svāhā
10.67.d: देवेभ्यस्स्वाहा । पितृभ्यस्स्वधाऽस्तु । भूतेभ्यो नमः । मनुष्येभ्यो हन्ता । प्रजापतये स्वाहा । परमेष्ठिने स्वाहा । यथा कूपः शतधारः सहस्रधारो अक्षितः । एवा मे अस्तु धान्यं सहस्रधारमक्षितम् । धनधान्यै स्वाहा । ये भूताः प्रचरन्ति दिवानक्तं बलिमिच्छन्तो वितुदस्य प्रेष्याः । तेभ्यो बलिं पुष्टिकामो हरामि मयि पुष्टिं पुष्टिपतिर्दधातु स्वाहा
10.67.m: To the gods, svāhā! To the fathers be svadhā! Homage to the beings! / To humans: hanta! To Prajāpati, svāhā! To Parameṣṭhin, svāhā! / As a well with a hundred streams, with a thousand streams, is inexhaustible, / so may my grain with a thousand streams be inexhaustible! To wealth and grain, svāhā! The beings who roam by day and night desiring an offering, the messengers of Vituda— / to them, desiring nourishment, I carry an offering; may the lord of nourishment bestow nourishment upon me, svāhā! / To herbs and trees, svāhā; to intermediate space, svāhā; homage to Rudra, lord of beasts, svāhā; the messengers of Vituda, and one.

10.68.s: oṃ tadbrahma | oṃ tadvāyuḥ | oṃ tadātmā | oṃ tathsatyam | oṃ tathsarvam | oṃ tatpurornamaḥ | antaścarati bhūteṣu guhāyāṃ viśvamūrtiṣu | tvaṃ yajñastvaṃ vaṣaṭkārastvamindrastvaṃ rudrastvaṃ viṣṇustvaṃ brahma tvaṃ prajāpatiḥ | tvaṃ tadāpa āpo jyotī raso'mṛtaṃ brahma bhūrbhuvassuvarom
10.68.d: ओं तद्ब्रह्म । ओं तद्वायुः । ओं तदात्मा । ओं तथ्सत्यम् । ओं तथ्सर्वम् । ओं तत्पुरोर्नमः । अन्तश्चरति भूतेषु गुहायां विश्वमूर्तिषु । त्वं यज्ञस्त्वं वषट्कारस्त्वमिन्द्रस्त्वं रुद्रस्त्वं विष्णुस्त्वं ब्रह्म त्वं प्रजापतिः । त्वं तदाप आपो ज्योती रसोऽमृतं ब्रह्म भूर्भुवस्सुवरोम्
10.68.m: Oṃ, that is brahman; Oṃ, that is Vāyu; Oṃ, that is the self; Oṃ, that is truth; Oṃ, that is all; / Oṃ, homage to that Puruṣa! He moves within all beings, in the cave, multiform. You are the sacrifice, you are the vaṣaṭ-call, you are Indra, you are Rudra, you are Viṣṇu, you are brahman, you are Prajāpati. You are those waters, waters, light, essence, immortal brahman, bhūr bhuvas suvar, oṃ!

10.69.s: śraddhāyāṃ prāṇe niviṣṭo'mṛtaṃ juhomi | śraddhāyāmapāne niviṣṭo'mṛtaṃ juhomi | śraddhāyāṃ vyāne niviṣṭo'mṛtaṃ juhomi | śraddhāyāmudāne niviṣṭo'mṛtaṃ juhomi | śraddhāyāṃ samāne niviṣṭo'mṛtaṃ juhomi | brahmaṇi ma ātmā'mṛtatvāya | amṛtopastaraṇamasi | śraddhāyāṃ prāṇe niviṣṭo'mṛtaṃ juhomi | śivo mā viśāpradāhāya | prāṇāya svāhā | śraddhāyāmapāne niviṣṭo'mṛtaṃ juhomi | śivo mā viśāpradāhāya | apānāya svāhā | śraddhāyāṃ vyāne niviṣṭo'mṛtaṃ juhomi | śivo mā viśāpradāhāya | vyānāya svāhā | śraddhāyāmudāne niviṣṭo'mṛtaṃ juhomi | śivo mā viśāpradāhāya | udānāya svāhā | śraddhāyāṃ samāne niviṣṭo'mṛtaṃ juhomi | śivo mā viśāpradāhāya | samānāya svāhā | brahmaṇi ma ātmā'mṛtatvāya | amṛtāpidhānamasi
10.69.d: श्रद्धायां प्राणे निविष्टोऽमृतं जुहोमि । श्रद्धायामपाने निविष्टोऽमृतं जुहोमि । श्रद्धायां व्याने निविष्टोऽमृतं जुहोमि । श्रद्धायामुदाने निविष्टोऽमृतं जुहोमि । श्रद्धायां समाने निविष्टोऽमृतं जुहोमि । ब्रह्मणि म आत्माऽमृतत्वाय । अमृतोपस्तरणमसि । श्रद्धायां प्राणे निविष्टोऽमृतं जुहोमि । शिवो मा विशाप्रदाहाय । प्राणाय स्वाहा । श्रद्धायामपाने निविष्टोऽमृतं जुहोमि । शिवो मा विशाप्रदाहाय । अपानाय स्वाहा । श्रद्धायां व्याने निविष्टोऽमृतं जुहोमि । शिवो मा विशाप्रदाहाय । व्यानाय स्वाहा । श्रद्धायामुदाने निविष्टोऽमृतं जुहोमि । शिवो मा विशाप्रदाहाय । उदानाय स्वाहा । श्रद्धायां समाने निविष्टोऽमृतं जुहोमि । शिवो मा विशाप्रदाहाय । समानाय स्वाहा । ब्रह्मणि म आत्माऽमृतत्वाय । अमृतापिधानमसि
10.69.m: Entered into faith, into the prāṇa breath, I offer the immortal. Entered into faith, into the apāna breath, I offer the immortal. Entered into faith, into the vyāna breath, I offer the immortal. Entered into faith, into the udāna breath, I offer the immortal. Entered into faith, into the samāna breath, I offer the immortal. In brahman is my self, for immortality. / You are the under-spreading of the immortal. Entered into faith, into the prāṇa breath, I offer the immortal; enter me auspiciously, without burning! To prāṇa, svāhā! Entered into faith, into the apāna breath, I offer the immortal; enter me auspiciously, without burning! To apāna, svāhā! Entered into faith, into the vyāna breath, I offer the immortal; enter me auspiciously, without burning! To vyāna, svāhā! / Entered into faith, into the udāna breath, I offer the immortal; enter me auspiciously, without burning! / To udāna, svāhā! Entered into faith, into the samāna breath, I offer the immortal; enter me auspiciously, without burning! To samāna, svāhā! In brahman is my self, for immortality. / You are the covering of the immortal.

10.70.s: śraddhāyāṃ prāṇe niviśyāmṛtaṃ hutam | prāṇamannenāpyāyasva | śraddhāyāmapāne niviśyāmṛtaṃ hutam | apānamannenāpyāyasva | śraddhāyāṃ vyāne niviśyāmṛtaṃ hutam | vyānamannenāpyāyasva | śraddhāyāmudāne niviśyāmṛtaṃ hutam | udānamannenāpyāyasva | śraddhāyāṃ samāne niviśyāmṛtaṃ hutam | samānamannenāpyāyasva
10.70.d: श्रद्धायां प्राणे निविश्यामृतं हुतम् । प्राणमन्नेनाप्यायस्व । श्रद्धायामपाने निविश्यामृतं हुतम् । अपानमन्नेनाप्यायस्व । श्रद्धायां व्याने निविश्यामृतं हुतम् । व्यानमन्नेनाप्यायस्व । श्रद्धायामुदाने निविश्यामृतं हुतम् । उदानमन्नेनाप्यायस्व । श्रद्धायां समाने निविश्यामृतं हुतम् । समानमन्नेनाप्यायस्व
10.70.m:
Having entered into faith, into the vital breath, the immortal [food] is offered; nourish the vital breath with food.
Having entered into faith, into the apāna breath, the immortal [food] is offered; nourish the apāna breath with food.
Having entered into faith, into the vyāna breath, the immortal [food] is offered; nourish the vyāna breath with food.
Having entered into faith, into the udāna breath, the immortal [food] is offered; nourish the udāna breath with food.
Having entered into faith, into the samāna breath, the immortal [food] is offered; nourish the samāna breath with food.

10.71.s: aṅguṣṭhamātraḥ puruṣo'ṅguṣṭhaṃ ca samāśritaḥ | īśassarvasya jagataḥ prabhuḥ prīṇāti viśvabhuk
10.71.d: अङ्गुष्ठमात्रः पुरुषोऽङ्गुष्ठं च समाश्रितः । ईशस्सर्वस्य जगतः प्रभुः प्रीणाति विश्वभुक्
10.71.m: The Puruṣa of the size of a thumb, having resorted to the thumb, the ruler of the whole world, the master, all-consuming, rejoices.

10.72.s: vāṅma āsann | nasoḥ prāṇaḥ | akṣyoścakṣuḥ | karṇayoḥ śrotram | bāhuvorbalam | ūruvorojaḥ | ariṣṭā viśvānyaṅgāni tanūḥ | tanuvā me saha namaste astu mā mā hiṃsīḥ
10.72.d: वाङ्म आसन्न् । नसोः प्राणः । अक्ष्योश्चक्षुः । कर्णयोः श्रोत्रम् । बाहुवोर्बलम् । ऊरुवोरोजः । अरिष्टा विश्वान्यङ्गानि तनूः । तनुवा मे सह नमस्ते अस्तु मा मा हिंसीः
10.72.m:
May speech [remain] in my mouth, the vital breath in my nostrils, sight in my eyes, hearing in my ears,
strength in my arms, vigor in my thighs, all my limbs uninjured, [and my] body!
Together with my body, homage be to you; do not harm me!

10.73.s: vayassuparṇā upasedurindraṃ priyamedhā ṛṣayo nādhamānāḥ | apa dhvāntamūrṇuhi pūrddhi cakṣurmumugdhyasmānnidhaye'va baddhān
10.73.d: वयस्सुपर्णा उपसेदुरिन्द्रं प्रियमेधा ऋषयो नाधमानाः । अप ध्वान्तमूर्णुहि पूर्द्धि चक्षुर्मुमुग्ध्यस्मान्निधयेऽव बद्धान्
10.73.m:
Like birds with beautiful wings, the seers, the Priyamedhas, approached Indra, seeking help:
"Dispel the darkness, fill our eyes [with light], release us who are bound as if in a snare!"

10.74.s: prāṇānāṃ granthirasi rudro mā viśāntakaḥ | tenānnenāpyāyasva
10.74.d: प्राणानां ग्रन्थिरसि रुद्रो मा विशान्तकः । तेनान्नेनाप्यायस्व
10.74.m:
You are the knot of the vital breaths; do not enter me as Rudra the end-maker.
By that food, be nourished!

10.75.m: Homage to Rudra, to Viṣṇu! Protect my death [from me]!

10.76.s: tvamagne dyubhistvamāśu śukṣaṇistvamadbhyastvamaśmanaspari | tvaṃ vanebhyastvamoṣadhībhyastvaṃ nṛṇāṃ nṛpate jāyase śuciḥ
10.76.d: त्वमग्ने द्युभिस्त्वमाशु शुक्षणिस्त्वमद्भ्यस्त्वमश्मनस्परि । त्वं वनेभ्यस्त्वमोषधीभ्यस्त्वं नृणां नृपते जायसे शुचिः
10.76.m:
You, Agni, [are born] with the days; you, swift, shining; you from the waters, you from the rock;
you from the forests, you from the plants; you, lord of men, are born pure among men.

10.77.s: śivena me santiṣṭhasva syonena me santiṣṭhasva subhūtena me santiṣṭhasva brahmavarcasena me santiṣṭhasva yajñasyarddhimanu santiṣṭhasvopa te yajña nama upa te nama upa te namaḥ
10.77.d: शिवेन मे सन्तिष्ठस्व स्योनेन मे सन्तिष्ठस्व सुभूतेन मे सन्तिष्ठस्व ब्रह्मवर्चसेन मे सन्तिष्ठस्व यज्ञस्यर्द्धिमनु सन्तिष्ठस्वोप ते यज्ञ नम उप ते नम उप ते नमः
10.77.m: Conclude auspiciously for me, conclude pleasantly for me, conclude with prosperity for me, conclude with spiritual luster for me, conclude according to the success of the sacrifice! Homage to you, sacrifice! Homage to you! Homage to you!

10.78.s: satyaṃ paraṃ paraṃ satyaṃ satyena na suvargāllokāccyavante kadācana satāṃ hi satyaṃ tasmāthsatye ramante tapa iti tapo nānaśanātparaṃ yaddhi paraṃ tapastaddurdharṣaṃ taddurādharṣaṃ tasmāttapasi ramante dama iti niyataṃ brahmacāriṇastasmāddame ramante śama ityaraṇye munayastamācchame ramante dānamiti sarvāṇi bhūtāni praśaṃsanti dānānnātiduścaraṃ tasmāddāne ramante dharma iti dharmeṇa sarvamidaṃ parigṛhītaṃ dharmānnāti duṣkaraṃ tasmāddharme ramante prajana iti bhūyāṃsastasmādbhūyiṣṭhāḥ prajāyante tasmādbhūyiṣṭhāḥ prajanane ramante'gnaya ityāha tasmādagnaya ādhātavyā agnihotramityāha tasmādagnihotre ramante yajña iti yajño hi devāstasmādyajñe ramante mānasamiti vidvāṃsastasmādvidvāṃsa eva mānase ramante nyāsa iti brahmā brahmā hi paraḥ paro hi brahmā tāni vā etānyavarāṇi parāṃsi nyāsa evātyarecayadya evaṃ vedetyupaniṣat

10.78.m: "Truth is supreme, supreme is truth! By truth they never fall from the world of heaven, for truth belongs to the virtuous; therefore they delight in truth." "Ascetic heat!" they say; there is no ascetic heat higher than fasting, for what is the highest ascetic heat is unassailable, is inviolable; therefore they delight in ascetic heat. "Restraint!" say the chaste students continuously; therefore they delight in restraint. "Tranquility!" say the sages in the forest; therefore they delight in tranquility. "Giving!" all beings praise; nothing is harder to surpass than giving; therefore they delight in giving. "Dharma!" they say; by dharma all this is encompassed; nothing is harder to surpass than dharma; therefore they delight in dharma. "Procreation!" say the many; therefore most beings are born; therefore the most delight in procreation. "The fires!" he says; therefore the fires are to be established. "The agnihotra!" he says; therefore they delight in the agnihotra. "Sacrifice!" they say; for the gods are the sacrifice; therefore they delight in sacrifice. "Mental [worship]!" say the wise; therefore the wise alone delight in mental [worship]. "Renunciation!" say they: [it is] Brahman, for Brahman is the supreme, and supreme is Brahman. Truly, all these other supreme [practices] renunciation surpassed. He who knows thus [attains this]. Such is the Upaniṣad.

10.79.m: Āruṇi Suparṇeya, descendant of Prajāpati, approached his father Prajāpati: 'What do the venerable ones declare to be supreme?' He said to him: 'By truth the wind blows; by truth Āditya shines in the sky; truth is the foundation of speech; on truth everything is established; therefore they declare truth to be supreme. By ascetic heat the gods attained godhead in the beginning; by ascetic heat the seers found heaven; by ascetic heat let us drive away rivals and enemies; on ascetic heat everything is established; therefore they declare ascetic heat to be supreme. By self-restraint the restrained shake off evil; by self-restraint Vedic students went to heaven; self-restraint is unassailable for living beings; on self-restraint everything is established; therefore they declare self-restraint to be supreme. By tranquility the tranquil practice what is auspicious; by tranquility the silent sages found the firmament; tranquility is unassailable for living beings; on tranquility everything is established; therefore they declare tranquility to be supreme. Giving is the defense of sacrifices, the priestly gift in the world; all beings subsist on the giver; by giving they drove away enemies; by giving foes become friends; on giving everything is established; therefore they declare giving to be supreme. Dharma is the foundation of the whole world; in the world beings approach the most righteous; by dharma one drives away evil; on dharma everything is established; therefore they declare dharma to be supreme. Procreation is indeed the foundation in the world; properly extending the thread of offspring, one becomes debt-free to the fathers; that indeed is one's debt-freedom; therefore they declare procreation to be supreme. The fires are indeed the threefold knowledge, the path of the gods; the Gārhapatya is the Ṛk, the earth, the Rathantara; the Anvāhāryapacana is the Yajus, the intermediate space, the Vāmadevya; the Āhavanīya is the Sāman, the world of heaven, the Bṛhat; therefore they declare the fires to be supreme. The Agnihotra in evening and morning is the expiation of households, well-sacrificed, well-offered, the beginning of sacrifice-rites, the light of the world of heaven; therefore they declare the Agnihotra to be supreme. "Sacrifice," they say, for by sacrifice the gods went to the sky; by sacrifice they drove away the asuras; by sacrifice foes become friends; on sacrifice everything is established; therefore they declare sacrifice to be supreme. The mental is indeed connected to Prajāpati, a purifier; with the mental mind one sees properly; the mental seers created creatures; on the mental everything is established; therefore they declare the mental to be supreme. Wise men declare renunciation to be brahman; brahman is the universe; which [is he]? The self-existent Prajāpati is the year. The year is that Āditya; he who is this person in Āditya is Parameṣṭhin, brahman, the Self. By the rays with which Āditya gives heat, Parjanya rains; by Parjanya herbs and trees are produced; by herbs and trees food comes to be; by food the vital breaths; by the vital breaths strength; by strength ascetic heat; by ascetic heat faith; by faith wisdom; by wisdom intellect; by intellect mind; by mind peace; by peace consciousness; by consciousness memory; by memory recollection; by recollection understanding; by understanding one causes the Self to be known; therefore giving food, one gives all these. From food come the vital breaths of living beings; by the vital breaths, mind; and from mind, understanding; from understanding, bliss; brahman is the womb. He indeed is this fivefold person, having five selves, by whom all this is interwoven: earth and intermediate space, sky, quarters, and intermediate directions. He indeed is all this world; he is the past, he the future; formed by desire to know, born of truth, dwelling in wealth, faith, true, glorious, superior to ascetic heat. Knowing him thus with mind and heart, as one who knows, do not again approach death. Therefore they declare renunciation to be superior to these ascetic heats. "A delightful treasure you are, all-pervading; in the vital breath you are the uniter; O brahman, you are the supporter of all; you are the giver of luster; you are Agni; you are the giver of splendor; you are of Sūrya; you are the giver of brilliance; you are of the moon. You are taken with a vessel; to you, to the greatness of brahman, [I offer]." With "Om" one should yoke oneself. This indeed is the great Upaniṣad, the secret of the gods; he who knows thus attains the greatness of brahman; therefore, the greatness of brahman. Thus the Upaniṣad.'

10.80.d: तस्यैवं विदुषो यज्ञस्यात्मा यजमानः श्रद्धा पत्नी शरीरमिध्ममुरो वेदिर्लोमानि बर्हिर्वेदः शिखा हृदयं यूपः काम आज्यं मन्युः पशुस्तपोऽग्निर्दमः शमयिता दक्षिणा वाग्घोता प्राण उद्गाता चक्षुरध्वर्युर्मनो ब्रह्मा श्रोत्रमग्नीद्यावद्ध्रियते सा दीक्षा यदश्नाति तद्धविर्यत्पिबति तदस्य सोमपानं यद्रमते तदुपसदो यथ्संचरत्युपविशत्युत्तिष्ठते च स प्रवर्ग्यो यन्मुखं तदाहवनीयो या व्याहृतिरहुतिर्यदस्य विज्ञानं तज्जुहोति यथ्सायं प्रातरत्ति तथ्समिधं यत्प्रातर्मध्यंदिनं सायं च तानि सवनानि ये अहोरात्रे ते दर्शपूर्णमासौ येऽर्धमासाश्च मासाश्च ते चातुर्मास्यानि य ऋतवस्ते पशुबन्धा ये संवथ्सराश्च परिवथ्सराश्च तेऽहर्गणाः सर्ववेदसं वा एतथ्सत्रं यन्मरणं तदवभृथ एतद्वै जरामर्यमग्निहोत्रं सत्रं य एवं विद्वानुदगयने प्रमीयते देवानामेव महिमानं गत्वा'ऽदित्यस्य सायुज्यं गच्छत्यथ यो दक्षिणे प्रमीयते पितृणामेव महिमानं गत्वा चन्द्रमसः सायुज्यं सलोकतामाप्नोत्येतौ वै सूर्याचन्द्रमसोर्महिमानौ ब्राह्मणो विद्वानभिजयति तस्माद्ब्रह्मणो महिमानमाप्नोति तस्माद्ब्रह्मणो महिमानम्
10.80.m:
For him who knows thus, of this sacrifice the self is the sacrificer, faith is the wife, the body is the kindling wood, the chest is the altar, the bodily hairs are the sacrificial grass, the Veda is the lock of hair, the heart is the sacrificial post, desire is the clarified butter, fury is the sacrificial animal, ascetic heat is the fire, self-restraint is the slaughterer, the sacrificial gift [is distributed], speech is the hotṛ, vital breath is the udgātṛ, the eye is the adhvaryu, the mind is the brahman, the ear is the agnīdh. As long as he lives, that is the consecration. What he eats, that is the oblation; what he drinks, that is his drinking of soma; when he amuses himself, that is the upasads; when he walks about, sits down, and rises up, that is the pravargya; what is his mouth, that is the āhavanīya; what utterance he makes, that is the offering; what his discernment is, that he pours out; what he eats evening and morning, that is the kindling wood; what he does in the morning, at midday, and in the evening, those are the pressings; what the days and nights are, they are the new- and full-moon sacrifices; what the half-months and months are, they are the four-month seasonal sacrifices; what the seasons are, they are the animal offerings; what the years and circular years are, they are the series of sacrificial days. This satra is indeed one where all one's possessions are given away; that death [comes], that is the concluding bath. This indeed is the Agnihotra satra that ends only with old age or death. The wise man who knows thus, dying during the sun's northern course, going indeed to the greatness of the gods, attains union with Āditya. Now, he who dies during the southern course, going indeed to the greatness of the fathers, attains union with the moon and attains the same world. These two glories of the sun and the moon the knowing brāhmaṇa conquers; therefore he attains the glory of brahman; therefore he attains the glory of brahman. [Thus is the Upaniṣad.]
